title: A communal catalogue reveals Earth’s multiscale microbial diversity
figures: Fig. 1b: sampling map; Fig. 2: diversity and ordination; Fig. 3a–b: ordered presence–absence matrices; Extended Data Fig. 3b: Procrustes comparison; Extended Data Fig. 5c–f: classification and source tracking.
lesson: Use consistent environmental categories to connect geographic, diversity and community views.

title: Structure and function of the global ocean microbiome
figures: Fig. 1a,c: map and gene accumulation; Fig. 3: ordination and depth comparisons; Fig. 4b: distance decay; Fig. 5b: environmental correlation matrix linked to community-distance associations; Fig. 6b: observed versus predicted temperature; Fig. 8a: aligned taxonomic and functional profiles.
lesson: Pair community patterns with environmental gradients and prediction checks.
verification: Primary article PDF and captions; Fig. 4–5 layouts visually inspected.

title: Marine DNA Viral Macro- and Microdiversity from Pole to Pole
figures: Fig. 1a–b: sampling map and length histograms; Fig. 2a: read-recruitment profiles; Fig. 3: ecological-scale schematic; Fig. 4a–b: PCoA and scatterplot with marginal boxplots; Fig. 6a: set overlap; Fig. 7: geographic and depth gradients.
lesson: Combine multivariate structure, marginal distributions and ecological context in one coordinated figure.
verification: Primary article PDF and captions; Fig. 4 layout visually inspected. Public PDF is an article-in-press version.

title: Structure and function of the global topsoil microbiome
figures: Fig. 1: matched diversity–latitude panels; Fig. 2a,c: correlation matrix and structural equation model; Extended Data Fig. 4: variable-importance/correlation dot matrices; Extended Data Fig. 5i–l: NMDS with environmental vectors.
lesson: Keep bacterial and fungal comparisons aligned while showing both response shape and environmental associations.
verification: Publisher-indexed captions and accepted-manuscript PDF; Fig. 1 layout visually inspected.

title: Determinants of community structure in the global plankton interactome
figures: Fig. 2a,d–g: association chord diagrams and geographic comparisons; Fig. 3b: aggregated network; Fig. 3e: sequence-context comparison; Fig. 4b–d: microscopy and three-dimensional reconstruction.
lesson: Connect association summaries to independent biological evidence and retain a clear definition of every edge.
verification: Primary article PDF and captions; Fig. 2 layout visually inspected.

title: A genomic catalog of Earth’s microbiomes
figures: Fig. 1b: genome-quality distributions; Fig. 3a: phylogeny with concentric metadata tracks; Fig. 4b: biosynthetic gene-cluster architecture; Fig. 5: host-link evidence and viral phylogeny.
lesson: Use a shared tree or genomic coordinate system to align multiple layers of annotation.
verification: Publisher-indexed text and primary full-text XML figure captions. Online publication was 2020; issue year is 2021.

title: A new view of the tree of life
figures: Fig. 1: broad phylogenetic overview of the tree of life.
lesson: Use overview trees to show evolutionary coverage, with readable clade summaries and focused detail views.
verification: Publisher article text; cited as a phylogenetic overview reference, without claiming a particular circular-track design.

title: Thousands of microbial genomes shed light on interconnected biogeochemical processes in an aquifer system
figures: Fig. 1: sampling scheme; Fig. 2: collapsed phylogeny; Fig. 3: rank-abundance displays; Fig. 4: annotated element cycles; Fig. 6: metabolic-handoff schematic.
lesson: Connect genome-derived metabolic potential to an explicit ecological model without calling it measured flux.

title: Ecogenomics and potential biogeochemical impacts of globally abundant ocean viruses
scope: Flagship; viral ecology and auxiliary metabolic genes
figures: Fig. 3a–b: pathway schematics; Extended Data Fig. 5–7: AMG phylogeny, abundance and genomic context, including P-II in Extended Data Fig. 7.
lesson: Link gene identity, genomic context, environmental distribution and metabolic interpretation.
verification: Publisher-indexed captions and author-manuscript figure legends.

title: High resolution time series reveals cohesive but short-lived communities in coastal plankton
figures: Fig. 1: taxonomic dynamics at different resolutions; Fig. 2: daily and smoothed trajectories; Fig. 3a–b: community dynamics aligned with environmental heatmaps.
lesson: Align biological and environmental time axes and distinguish short-term fluctuations from longer trends.
verification: Publisher-indexed captions and primary full-text XML.

title: Highly multiplexed spatial mapping of microbial communities
scope: Flagship; host-associated spatial microbiology, transferable to environmental imaging
figures: Fig. 2b–g: segmented cells, pair-correlation functions and volumetric views; Fig. 3a,f: labelled images and spatial association networks; Fig. 4: oral biofilm spatial organization.
lesson: Pair cell-level images with quantitative spatial summaries; distinguish fields of view from biological replicates.
verification: Primary full-text XML figure captions. Environmental applications in this catalogue are transfers from host-associated examples.

title: Microbial single-cell RNA sequencing by split-pool barcoding
scope: Flagship; cultured bacterial single-cell method, transferable to environmental isolates
figures: Fig. 1: method schematic, species-mixing quality-control scatter and t-SNE visualization.
lesson: Use embeddings to explore measured cell-state heterogeneity and show technical validation alongside them.
verification: Primary article and PubMed-indexed figure captions; t-SNE verified, not UMAP. Online publication was 2020; issue year is 2021.

title: A global atlas of soil viruses reveals unexplored biodiversity and potential biogeochemical impacts
figures: Fig. 1a: sampling map; Fig. 3a–c: cumulative distribution, host phylogeny with abundance rings and environmental correlation heatmap; Fig. 4: annotated cellular metabolic pathways; Extended Data Fig. 1: rarefaction.
lesson: Integrate geography, host evidence and functional potential with complementary encodings.

title: Biogeographic patterns and drivers of soil viromes
figures: Fig. 4a–b: network modules, regional/biome subnetworks and degree-distribution comparisons with model networks. The study also reports global diversity predictions.
lesson: Keep comparative network definitions and display rules consistent across regions.
verification: Publisher Fig. 4 caption and primary article abstract; prediction-map recipe is labelled as an adaptation.

title: UpSet: Visualization of Intersecting Sets
journal: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics
figures: Set-membership matrix linked to intersection sizes and set sizes.
lesson: Make many-set intersections comparable through aligned quantitative encodings.
verification: Original method paper; this is not a Nature, Science or Cell publication.

title: Complex heatmaps reveal patterns and correlations in multidimensional genomic data
figures: Parallel heatmaps, annotations and shared ordering.
lesson: Use coordinated matrix tracks to integrate heterogeneous measurements.
verification: Original method paper and author-maintained documentation; not a Nature, Science or Cell publication.

title: The misuse of colour in science communication
figures: Scientific colour-map examples and selection guidance.

title: Raincloud plots: a multi-platform tool for robust data visualization
figures: Raw observations, density and summary statistics in a coordinated distribution display.
lesson: Show the data distribution and observations alongside a summary.
verification: Original publication in 2019; the accessible PMC record also includes a revised 2021 version. Not a Nature, Science or Cell publication.

title: MOFA+: a statistical framework for comprehensive integration of multi-modal single-cell data
figures: Multi-modal latent factors and feature weights; environmental use is an adaptation.
lesson: Separate shared sample variation from the features contributing to it.
verification: Original method paper; not a Nature, Science or Cell publication.
